notes:
Your documents now have a proper home on the phone. It opens on whatever is still missing, you pick what each file is, and you see the file before it goes anywhere. Several can go up in one trip, each filed under its own heading, so three missing documents are three taps rather than three visits. Replacing one works the way it should: until HR has checked a document you simply swap it yourself, and once they have, your replacement goes to them as a request — and that request now sits on the document it is for, instead of vanishing the moment you send it and leaving you to wonder whether it arrived.

HR gets the whole desk on the phone too: everything an employee has put on file and everything issued to them, each carrying the decision that was made about it and the words that went with it. Replacement requests have their own tab and the decided ones are kept, so you can still see what was swapped in last March, or why one was sent back.

Documents are also called what they are actually called now — a Passport Size Photo is a Passport Size Photo, not a name split at the capitals.

Picking a PDF out of Downloads or Drive no longer fails. Android often hands the app a file without saying what kind it is, and the upload was turned away as an unsupported type the person had never chosen; it now reads the filename instead. A file with brackets in its name goes up as well.

A job can be open in more than one place. Add every location to the opening and the application form asks the candidate which one they are applying for, so a role running in three branches stops looking like a role in one. The branch travels with the candidate — on their row, on their record, and on your interview card, so a panel sitting for three cities at once knows which one the call is about. You choose it too when you add somebody by hand.

And somebody you have already turned down is now flagged the moment they come back. The flag opens into the earlier application: which opening and branch it was for, when it was rejected and by whom, the reason given, and every round of that attempt with its ratings, strengths, concerns and recommendation — so nobody sits through an interview asking the questions a panel has already answered. A rejection is kept for three months: inside that window the public form will not take another application for the same opening and tells the applicant the date they can try again, and after it they are free to apply. Turning somebody down now asks you why, because that is the line the next person to meet them will read.
